svg.title: Internal coherence can precede stable environmental anchoring (schematic)
svg.desc: Two panels. A: four polar plots of head-direction tuning (angle: head direction relative to a fixed room reference at the top; radius: normalized firing rate). Before eye opening, three cells' curves rotate together by the same angle between two observations, preserving their relative directions (shared drift). After eye opening, a separate ensemble of three cells keeps nearly the same room alignment. B: a qualitative developmental timeline with three overlapping bands: head direction present before eye opening (coherent relations, later more stable room alignment), place firing present by early exploration and refining later, and stable grid periodicity developing later. Band order is not a causal chain.

g.text: A: Internal coherence and external anchoring
Angle: head direction · Radius: normalized firing rate
Separate schematic ensembles; cell identities kept within each pair
Preferred directions more stable relative to the room
Qualitative synthesis; intervals and band edges are not measured ages.
Unfilled intervals do not establish absence of a response.
Developmental order does not establish a chain of causes.
